AI-native changes who executes — and who decides.
The decisive shift is from people carrying every handoff to people setting direction, defining requirements and resolving material exceptions while agents and software execute continuously. The gap between human-speed handoffs and machine-speed systems compounds.
Automation is not the answer to every process. The first decision is what to preserve, simplify, automate, rebuild or retire — and where a person must stay responsible.

units.authorityHeading: ## Transformation 2 - A different division of work
units.exactText:
Machine speed requires a different division of work.
An AI-native company does not merely give every employee a faster tool. It changes where execution sits. Agents and software can carry stable paths continuously; people set direction, define requirements, resolve material exceptions and verify what the system produces.
That division is never absolute. Judgment stays where consequence, ambiguity or accountability makes it valuable. The operating model must say where the machine may act, where it must stop and who owns the decision when it does.

See the whole path
See the whole path, not only the visible workflow.
We map the steps people can name and the work around them: waiting, rework, exceptions, approvals, systems, knowledge and decisions made more than once. Those handoffs often determine the speed and quality of the company more than the task at the center.
The map is built from operating evidence where it exists, then tested with the people who own the work. It becomes the basis for a decision, not a decorative process diagram.

units.exactText: Five outcomes, from keeping the work to stopping it

The strategic decision
The first decision is what not to automate.
Every mapped path is tested against five outcomes. Building is one possible result, never the premise.

Preserve
Keep the work as it is when the effort is proportionate to its value and human judgment is the point of the work.

units.authorityHeading: ## Transformation 4 - Choose the intervention / Simplify, Automate, Rebuild, Retire
units.exactText:
Simplify
Remove steps, approvals or transfers that no longer protect a material outcome before encoding the process in software.
Automate
Let agents execute a stable path when inputs, rules, exceptions and success criteria can be made explicit.
Rebuild
Redesign the workflow and its software together when the current system preserves the wrong operating model.
Retire
Stop doing work that no longer changes a decision, protects a requirement or serves the customer.
See how the intervention becomes a build

Sequence the change while the company keeps running.
The target operating model may be large. The first intervention should not be. We sequence bounded moves that create evidence, preserve a way back and make the next decision better informed.
For an existing company, this is a migration from accumulated systems and habits. For a new company, product, work, roles, data and software can be designed together from the beginning. The underlying discipline is the same.

Keep the operating model governable beyond any one model.
Dagg treats the model as one part of the harness. Company-specific context, tools, permissions, evaluations and records are designed as governable parts of the company's system rather than as intelligence trapped in one prompt or provider.
This is an architecture principle, not a promise of universal portability. Exact model providers, hosting, data residency, retention, encryption, access control, isolation and contractual commitments are established in technical diligence and the agreement.

Start technical diligence
See the governed build

A release needs a way back.
Each build defines how the capability can be disabled, how work returns to an approved manual or previous path, and who may make that decision. Evaluation of that reversal should be proportionate to the consequence of the action.
Technical diligence should resolve the exact data sources, model and provider choices, roles, environments, retention, access controls, evaluations, monitoring, incident responsibilities and contractual boundaries for the engagement.

Start an assessment
The first engagement is a decision, not a project.
An assessment follows one consequential workflow or operating decision, end to end, and decides what should be preserved, simplified, automated, rebuilt or retired.
